property_summary: After create() is called by a programOperator, c.owner() returns the address that was used to call create() (i.e., msg.sender).
After calling c.updateRoundImplementation() with a non-zero address, c.roundImplementation() returns that address.
The owner() function returns the address of the contract deployer before any ownership transfer.
After create() is called by a program operator, the owner can still call transferOwnership without reverting
After create() is called, the owner of the contract remains unchanged.
After a call to create() by a program operator, the owner of the contract remains the original deployer (address(this)).
After create() is called by a program operator, the owner (as returned by owner()) remains the address that was set during initialization (address(this) in setUp).

After any successful call to create(bytes,address) by a caller who is both a program operator and the current owner, the following call to transferOwnership(some address that is not the zero address) succeeds.
After calling create() with any valid parameters, the owner of the clone is not the zero address.
After calling create() with any valid parameters, the owner of the contract C (accessed via owner()) is not the zero address.
After any call to create(), the owner of the factory contract remains the original owner.
After any call to transferOwnership(newOwner), the owner of the contract is newOwner if the caller is owner, otherwise the owner remains unchanged.
After any call to create() with the caller being the owner of C, the owner of C remains unchanged.
transferOwnership should revert when the new owner is the zero address.
After a call to create(bytes,address) that reverts, the owner of the contract remains unchanged from the previous owner.
transferOwnership must prevent setting owner to address(0) by reverting.
After a successful call to create(bytes,address), the value of owner() does not become address(0).
After a successful call to create(bytes,address), the owner of the round contract clone is not address(0).
After calling create() with any valid arguments, the roundImplementation address stored in the contract is the address from which the clone was created.

After a call to create(), the roundImplementation state variable is always the address that was set by a previous updateRoundImplementation() call (i.e., roundImplementation only changes via updateRoundImplementation()).
After create() is called, the roundImplementation state variable is always equal to the address that was set by the last updateRoundImplementation() call.
After a successful create() call, roundImplementation remains unchanged if updateRoundImplementation was called before.
After a call to create() with encodedParameters and ownedBy, the value of roundImplementation is the same as before the call.
After create() returns, the alloSettings state variable is updated to the value passed via updateAlloSettings()
After create() is called, alloSettings retains the value set by the last updateAlloSettings call.
After create() returns, alloSettings remains equal to the value set by the previous updateAlloSettings call.
After creating a round via create(), alloSettings is unchanged from before the call, but the buggy contract does not update alloSettings, so it stays at its initially zero value.
After updateAlloSettings is called and then create is called, the value of alloSettings in the contract is the value set by updateAlloSettings.
The alloSettings address should equal the argument passed to updateAlloSettings after a round is created via create().
After a call to create() returns, the alloSettings address is not zero.
After a round is created via create(), the alloSettings address stored in the contract must equal the address set by the last updateAlloSettings call.
After each successful call to create(), the alloSettings state variable is not zero.
After a successful call to create(bytes,address), the alloSettings state variable is unchanged from its value before the call.
After a call to create with any valid encodedParameters and ownedBy, calling c.initialize() does not revert
After a call to create with any valid encodedParameters and ownedBy, the initialize getter should return true.
After a successful call to create() by an authorized program operator, the roundImplementation state variable must be non-zero.
After calling create with valid parameters by an authorized operator, c.owner() equals the ownedBy parameter.
After a call to create() succeeds, the value returned by c.owner() must be equal to the ownedBy parameter.
After a call to create(bytes,address) via an authorized program operator, the new round's address should equal the value stored in roundImplementation at that moment.
The cloned contract's implementation should be the current roundImplementation address.
After a successful call to create(), the value returned by roundImplementation() must equal the value stored prior to the call (as read from the getter).
For any authorized caller, the roundImplementation address never changes after a call to create().

After any successful call to create() by an authorized program operator, the address returned by roundImplementation() must equal the address of the implementation parameter used in the clone creation (which is the value stored before the call).
The address returned by create() must be different from the roundImplementation address set before the call.
The address returned by create() must be the address where a new contract was deployed (i.e., it must have code length > 0).

The address returned by create() must have code length strictly greater than the roundImplementation address, because a cloned contract is a new copy of the implementation, not the implementation itself.
The address returned by create() must differ from the predetermined clone address before initialization, i.e., it must be a new contract deployed via CREATE, not the roundImplementation itself.
The address returned by create() must have non-zero code length before the initialize call.
